answer: Multi‑head attention is a mechanism in which the single attention operation is split into several parallel “heads.” Each head projects the queries, keys and values into a lower‑dimensional space (for example, with d_k = d_v = d_model/h = 64) and performs its own attention calculation. The outputs of all heads are then concatenated and linearly transformed to produce the final result. This design keeps the overall computational cost roughly the same as a single‑head attention with full dimensionality, because each head works on a smaller sub‑space. The benefit of using multiple heads is that each one can focus on different aspects of the input, learning distinct patterns or relationships that would be harder to capture with a single attention function. By combining these diverse representations, multi‑head attention provides a richer, more expressive encoding of the sequence while also mitigating the loss of resolution that can occur when a single attention head averages over many positions.
